key_insight: This study will compare multiple large language models against expert human benchmarks for primary care advice quality and safety in Kenya, Malawi, and Tanzania.
clinical_relevance: It addresses whether LLMs can provide contextually appropriate, safe clinical decision support in low-resource primary healthcare settings.
method: Clinicians create 200–250 realistic hypothetical vignettes per country and write a human benchmark care plan.
Six open-source and proprietary LLMs are prompted with the same vignettes.
Expert clinicians compare masked LLM and human responses across soundness, safety, contextual fit, clarity, completeness, and confidence.
evidence_signal: The protocol requires at least 358 evaluations per LLM per country, enabling a fully crossed repeated-measures comparative validation.
watch_item: Results from hypothetical vignettes may not fully predict real-world performance in busy primary care settings or across all local languages and workflows.
paper_title: Evaluating large language models as clinical decision support tools in primary healthcare settings: Protocol for a multi-country comparative validation study on expert-adjudicated hypothetical vignettes (hypMOOVE-PHC)
